name: AICW World Championship
aka: American Internet Championship Wrestling World Championship
epitaph: Crowned in an eight-man ladder match at Apocalypse '97, where "The Demon" Kyle Bane became the fed's own first-ever World Champion. "Hard Line" Byron Brady dethroned him in a steel cage at New Year's Revolution; a masked debutant billed only as The Saint won it from Bane a second time at the Tokyo Thunder Festival, in a match decided by Byron Brady's own disguised interference as the Demonweb's "Legion"; Brady reclaimed it from The Saint at Steel City Meltdown, the belt's own last recorded change in the surviving record.
notes: The belt's own name drifts between "World Championship" and "World Heavyweight Championship" across the held record without the fed itself ever marking a rename; recorded as one continuous lineage.

name: AICW Television Championship
epitaph: AICW's own first title, awarded at a seven-man gauntlet on Fright Night to "Swingin'" Chandler Stone. The belt changes hands repeatedly across the surviving record — to Elvis, to Stephon T. Davis, to "Pretty Boy" Troy Walcott, to "The Convict" Oswald Bates, and, after an off-page saga involving a voided win and a Commissioner's own fiat award, to Legion and then Zeek Monkey — several of its own transitions never shown on any served card.
notes: One document (Steel City Meltdown) names a physical belt "the AICW Extreme title"/"jobber title" in what its own surrounding text treats as this same lineage; not clearly resolved in the surviving record, so recorded here rather than as a separate title.

name: AICW International Championship
epitaph: Crowned at Apocalypse '97 in the "King of the Hill" battle royal — two simultaneous eleven-man battle royals whose survivors met in a singles final, won by "8-Ball" Vic Garibaldi. The belt passes to Mista Smith and then to "The Ultimate Male" Chris Del Rio off-page, in transitions the surviving record never shows, before Gino Valentini wins it from Del Rio at Steel City Meltdown, the belt's own last recorded change.

name: AICW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Crowned at Apocalypse '97 in a tag tournament final won by the Nubian Warriors, Nelson and Muffasa Bukola. The Perfectly Perfect Duo, Lance and Max Studd, dethroned them at Seasons Beatings/Violent Night and held the belts through the whole of the surviving record after — five months and counting by the fed's own last-recorded show.

name: AICW Inoki Cup
epitaph: An eight-man single-elimination tournament staged across the Tokyo Thunder Festival's own two nights, won by "Big D" Devon Burke over Rory Christianson in the final. Burke defended the cup successfully the same event, against Vic Garibaldi, and is still billed champion in the fed's own last-recorded show.
notes: Born from a one-time tournament but billed and defended afterward as an ongoing championship, not a single trophy.

name: AICW North American Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Named once in the surviving record: the Asian Assassination Squad, Blackjack Takahashi and Thripaq Nguyen, are billed as champions on AICW's own Survival of the Fittest. No document shows the title being won, defended, or lost.
